page.layout: One page of running text, with one marginal note in the left margin at the first line. Faint marks in the left margin lower down are not legible and are described under notes. No headers except the running head.

main_text.p: meam, Coriscum, Erastum, viros eximios, gravissimé hortatur, ut in eam rem certatim incumbant, ut concordibus animis in unum quen-dam unius amicitiæ complexum, unamq; communitatem mutuis ne-xibus coalescant. Et in Dialogis suis sapientissimis passim κοινωνίαν καὶ συμπαλοχὴν[?] hanc, & concordem germanitatem perquam magnificé & splendidissimis verbis commendat. Quæ ut olim magna cum volupta-te mente complexus sum: sic quoties, CASPAR PEVCERE, vir eximie, memoria & cogitatione mecum repeto atq; recolligo: toties opti-morum quondam Procerum & Doctorum, adeoq; pulcerrimi cœtus, & universæ Reipubl. Scholasticæ in Academia Witebergensi status memoria, non animo modo, sed prope oculis meis obversatur. Etenim ea habuit inde usq; ab initio, suo quodam peculiari fato, & Dei perbe-nigno concessu, cum alia multa singularia, antequam alvei illius mi-serè perturbarentur & disjicerentur, tum vero hoc maximè, quod in docetibus τὸ ὅμοιον καὶ ξύμφωνον[?] illud semper fuit, hoc est, voluntatum inter eos consensio, arctissima animorum colligatio, copulatioq; in Deo, & ὁμοδοξία[?]: auditorum vero atq; discentium ea erga præceptores suos & erga se mutuo affectio, ut ubicunq; postea, etiam multorum annorum spatio decurso, vel cōgressi sunt superioribus annis, vel etiamnum conveniunt priores illi Witebergenses, non nisi cum summa animi lætitia inter se amare & complecti cernas. Fuit & admirabilis pené omnium, qui vel docuerunt, vel didicerunt in ea Schola, ut in alijs, ita & in sermonis genere & charactere dicendi, una tanquam Musica, hoc est congruentia & similitudo. Perfecit id sua dexteritate, sapien-tia, suavitate vocis, & penna bonitate, quibus ornatus & auctorita-te, qua armatus fuit à Deo, pené inimitabili, MAGnus[?] ille Philippus Melanchthon, socer tuus, beatissimæ memoriæ: Qui fuit feré primus & communis præceptor, atq; ceu οἰκοδεσπότης[?], & magister ac instaurator cum omnium aliarum doctrinarum in Germania, tum vero etiam studiorum eloquentiæ, quæ ipse & magno conatu excitabat & propagabat, bene favente Deo, felicissimè: cum quidem & primis & posteri-oribus temporibus solus feré adornaret ac scriberet, quæ propone-banturInEpist.6.ep.

page.notes: The catchword "bantur" stands at the right below the last line and is not repeated in the text. No page number is clearly legible at the head; a faint mark there was not read and is left out. Greek: κοινωνίαν and οἰκοδεσπότης are read with doubt; "συμπαλοχὴν" (perhaps συμπλοκὴν), "ξύμφωνον" and "ὁμοδοξία" are marked [?]. A blot covers the letters after "MA" in "Magnus", so the reading is uncertain. The left margin has faint, illegible traces of further text beside lines 9 to 12 and near line 22, probably show-through or stamps, and are not transcribed. The top of the leaf has a stain. The Greek sign in "Academia" is a printed ornament and is not transcribed as text.
